title: Enemy
description:
A creature the party fights. DELIBERATELY THREE WEIGHTS, because a fight made only of full stat blocks is a fight nobody finishes: most enemies are an AC, some hit points and two attacks, and that is the whole of them. Kayki: "some enemies just have attacks, AC and HP, nothing else; some have 1 feature, some have more, and the bosses will have class and features."

NOTHING HERE IS ROLLED BY THE APP. The numbers are what a DM reads off a card — this system's app is a tracker, not a referee (RULES.md). The one thing the app does with an enemy is put it on the board with its hit points already filled in.

WHAT AN ENEMY DOES NOT HAVE: levels, ability score improvements, an engine, tricks with cooldowns, or a character sheet. A boss BORROWS a class's identity and a handful of its features, written out here in full — it never resolves against the class data, because a boss is a one-off and a class is a twenty-level ladder.

DEFENCE, AND IT IS DECIDED BY TIER (Kayki, 2026-08-11): **specials and bosses Parry; normal enemies do not.** Every enemy has an AC and an attack must meet or beat it; a `normal` then simply takes the hit, which is what keeps a room of six moving — six mobs each rolling a Parry is six more d20 rolls a round. A `special` or a `boss` carries a `parryDC` and Parries exactly as a player does (MECHANICS §1): a flat d20 against it, above takes nothing, on it takes half, below takes half again as much.

id.description: kebab-case unique id; defaults to slug of name

flavor.description: One line: what it looks like across a dark ring. This is the first thing a DM reads out.

tier.description:
The three weights.
  normal  — an AC, some hit points, one or two attacks, and AT MOST one small trait. Several appear at once. Killed in a round or two.
  special — a fight's second gear: more hit points, a signature move, one or two features, usually a condition it can inflict. One or two per fight.
  boss    — carries a CLASS and a handful of its features plus unique moves of its own. One per fight, and the fight is about it.

size.description: Drives how many squares its figure covers on the board: Large is 2, Huge is 3.

kind.description: What sort of thing it is, in this world's own words — 'performer', 'beast', 'rigging', 'crowd'. Free text on purpose: a creature-type table is a taxonomy nobody asked for.

partyLevel.description: The band of party levels this is written for, e.g. '1-3'. Not a CR: this system has no encounter-building maths and inventing one here would be inventing a rule.

acNote.description: What the AC IS, in a word or two — 'padded coat', 'greasepaint and nerve', 'plate and rigging'. A number with no reason behind it is a number a DM cannot improvise around.

hpDice.description: The dice the hit points come from, e.g. '4d8+8' — for a DM who prefers to roll them.

otherSpeeds.description: Anything besides walking: 'climb 30 ft', 'fly 40 ft (rigging only)'.

parryDC.description: Specials and bosses only. It Parries exactly as a player does — a flat d20 against this DC, lower is better, costing its reaction (MECHANICS §1). A normal enemy has none and simply takes the hit, which is what keeps a room of six moving.

resist.description: Damage types it takes half of.

immune.description: Damage types and conditions it ignores entirely.

vulnerable.description: Damage types it takes double of. The lever that makes a party's odd trick suddenly the right answer.

senses.description: Anything beyond ordinary sight: 'blindsight 30 ft', 'hears everything within 60 ft'.

toHit.description: Added to the d20 against the target's AC.

damage.description: Fixed dice, e.g. '1d6+2'. An enemy's damage does not scale with anything — it is written down.

note.description: The rider, if it has one: a save, a condition, a shove.

multiattack.description: One line saying how many attacks it makes on its turn and which. Omit for one attack.

uses.description: '1 / combat', '1 / turn', 'passive' — the same vocabulary a class feature uses.

from.description: BOSSES ONLY: the class this feature is borrowed from, named so the table can see what it is fighting.

borrowsClass.description: BOSSES ONLY. The class id whose identity this boss wears ('joker', 'illusionist'). It borrows a HANDFUL of features, written out in full above — it does not resolve against the class data, because a boss is a one-off and a class is a twenty-level ladder.

tactics.description: How to PLAY it — what it opens with, what it does when hurt, what it will not do. The half of a stat block that makes a fight feel like something, and the half most stat blocks leave out.

narration.description: In play: what the table sees and hears when it acts. No numbers.
